title: Source tax tariff: children
purpose: For employees subject to source tax only, ask whether there are children, then one block of questions per child. Each block asks only what is needed to decide whether that child counts towards the tariff digit or leads to tariff H.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: the employee to say whether they (or, if married, they or their spouse) have biological or adopted children, asked only when the employee is subject to source tax and has earned income
stories.so_that: the Zurich tariff calculator's children questions can be answered without follow-up emails, while employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked about their family (data minimisation)
stories.priority_reason: Without this answer the source tax tariff cannot be determined; HR today cannot tell up front who must answer source tax questions, and data minimisation forbids asking everyone (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's answers on residence, nationality, permit and spouse decide whether they are subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax, owned by another section) and they have earned income
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the children question is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax; employees who are not subject never see it

examples.name: Married B-permit holder with a non-Swiss spouse

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked for replacement income
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose income type is replacement income
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax questions are asked
acceptance_criteria.then: the children question is not asked, because the calculator skips all personal and child questions for replacement income (see OQ-income-type on whether a new employee can have replacement income at all)

acceptance_criteria.title: Position and scope of the question depend on civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with earned income
acceptance_criteria.then: for a married employee it comes after the question whether the spouse works and covers biological or adopted children of the employee or the spouse; for an employee who is not married it comes after the denomination question and covers the employee's own biological or adopted children

acceptance_criteria.title: Answer yes or no; yes opens the per-child questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is "yes" or "no" and cannot be left empty; only "yes" leads to the per-child questions, "no" asks nothing about children; the answer is needed by the source tax office (Zurich calculator)

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: for every child the employee declares, to know whether the child is a minor, an adult in first education or neither, and (for the first two) whether the child lives in the employee's household
stories.so_that: children who cannot count towards the tariff are dropped right away and the remaining questions for each child can be narrowed down
stories.priority_reason: These answers decide for every child whether it counts towards the source tax tariff; without them the tariff cannot be determined.

acceptance_criteria.title: A block of questions for each child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered "yes" to having biological or adopted children (US-07.1)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can describe each child in its own block (Child 1, Child 2, ...) and can add or remove a child; every question of this section is answered per child. How the calculator behaves with more than three children or after removing a child was not checked (see OQ-calculator-coverage)

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status asked for every child
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say whether the child is "Minor", "Adult in first education" or "Neither"; the question cannot be left empty and is needed by the source tax office

acceptance_criteria.title: A child who is neither ends its block
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Neither" (not a minor and not an adult in first education)
acceptance_criteria.then: no further question is asked for that child, and the child does not count towards the tariff

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household asked for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Minor" or "Adult in first education"
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to whether the child lives in the same household; it is needed by the source tax office to decide whether and how the child counts

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: for a minor child living in the employee's household, to know the parental custody and, only where it matters, the common household with the other parent, alternating custody and who pays more of the child's maintenance
stories.so_that: it can be decided whether the child counts towards the tariff digit and, for employees who are not married, whether it leads to tariff H
stories.priority_reason: Needed for a correct tariff, but only for employees subject to source tax with a minor child at home; no source names a specific incident.

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody asked; sole custody ends the block
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Minor" who lives in the same household (US-07.2)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must choose "Shared custody" or "Sole custody"; with sole custody no further question is asked for that child (the child counts, and for an employee who is not married it leads to tariff H)

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody: common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child in the household with shared custody
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to living in a common household with the child's other parent. With "yes", a married employee is asked nothing more for that child (the child counts), and an employee who is not married is asked who pays more of the child's maintenance (alternating custody is not asked)

given.value: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

acceptance_criteria.title: No common household: alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child in the household with shared custody, where the employee does not live in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to alternating custody; with "no" nothing more is asked for that child

examples.name: Single, no common household, no alternating custody (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc0ae9)
Married, no common household, no alternating custody (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-a4d358)

given.value: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

acceptance_criteria.title: Alternating custody: who pays more of the maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child in the household with alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance: "The employee" or "The other parent"; it is needed by the source tax office to decide whether the child counts

given.value: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

stories.title: Minor child not living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: for a minor child who does not live with the employee, to know about shared custody (married employees) or parental care (employees who are not married) and, only where it matters, alternating custody and who pays more of the maintenance
stories.so_that: it can be decided whether a child living elsewhere still counts towards the tariff, without asking questions that do not apply
stories.priority_reason: Needed for a correct tariff, but only for employees subject to source tax with a minor child living elsewhere; no source names a specific incident.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employee: shared custody
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee subject to source tax with a child described as "Minor" who does not live in the same household
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to shared custody; the parental-care and in-household custody questions are not asked

examples.name: Married, child elsewhere, no shared custody (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc6ace)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee not married: parental care
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is single, divorced or widowed, with a child described as "Minor" who does not live in the same household
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to having parental care; the shared-custody question for married employees is not asked

examples.name: Single, child elsewhere, no parental care (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc6ace)

acceptance_criteria.title: With shared custody or parental care: alternating custody, then maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child not in the household, where the married employee has shared custody or the employee who is not married has parental care
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to alternating custody; only with "yes" are they asked who pays more of the child's maintenance ("The employee" or "The other parent"). Without shared custody or parental care (AC-07.4.1, AC-07.4.2) the child does not count and nothing more is asked

examples.name: Married, shared custody, alternating, employee pays more (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc6ace)
Single, parental care, alternating, employee pays more (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc6ace)
Single, parental care, no alternating custody

stories.title: Adult child in first education
stories.i_want: for an adult child in first education, to know whether the employee shares a household with the other parent and, where needed, whether the employee pays more than 50% of the child's maintenance or is the main financial contributor
stories.so_that: it can be decided whether the adult child counts towards the tariff and, for employees who are not married, whether it leads to tariff H
stories.priority_reason: Needed for a correct tariff, but only for employees subject to source tax with an adult child in first education; no source names a specific incident.

acceptance_criteria.title: In the household: common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Adult in first education" who lives in the same household (US-07.2)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to living in a common household with the child's other parent; no custody or alternating-custody question is asked for an adult child. With "yes", a married employee is asked nothing more for that child (the child counts), and an employee who is not married is asked who pays more of the child's maintenance

examples.name: Married, adult child at home, common household (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-3eb561)
Single, adult child at home, common household

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 50% of the maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Adult in first education" who either does not live in the same household, or lives there without a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they mainly (more than 50%) pay for the child's maintenance; the child counts only with "yes". The common-household question is not asked for a child outside the household

examples.name: Single, adult child at home, no common household (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-3eb561)
